body: Step 1 says `bin/wt-remove <slug> --if-empty` removes the worktree and its local branch. That is not true on this path. `bin/wt-new` already pushed the branch, so `refs/remotes/origin/<slug>` still exists when wt-remove runs. Its `! show-ref --verify refs/remotes/origin/$BRANCH` guard then skips `branch -D`. Step 2 deletes the remote branch afterwards, but the local branch stays behind. That leftover branch trips wt-new's existing-branch guard on a same-slug retry, which is the case the new deletion code was written to stop. Fix one of two ways: delete the remote branch first and run `git fetch --prune` before wt-remove, or add an explicit `git branch -D <slug>` after the remote delete.

body: The new step 1 tells the agent to run `cd /Users/ajaynicolas/GitHub/IBL5 && bin/wt-remove <slug> --if-empty`. That is a `cd` plus `&&` chain into the main checkout, and the global CLAUDE.md says worktree-isolated sessions get this exact shape blocked. If the hook blocks it, the agent never reaches the `kept` branch. It then has no defined outcome, and an empty worktree is left behind. Use the worktree's own copy of the script, or a form the hooks allow such as `git -C`.
